title: Wisdom Literature
description: The Bible's wisdom corpus in an order that builds: Proverbs states the rule, Job presses the exception, Ecclesiastes tests the limits, the Song celebrates love, and the Psalms and James carry wisdom into prayer and practice.
audience: A reader drawn to the Bible's reflective books who wants them to talk to each other instead of reading them in isolation.

sequence.note: The foundation: the fear of the LORD, and Wisdom calling in the streets.
The rule: how life usually works under God. Patterns, not promises — remember that for Job.
Humility before the rule: Agur's riddles, and wisdom embodied in a household.
The Psalter opens as a wisdom book: two ways to live.
Wisdom as delight: the great acrostic love poem to God's word.
Now the exception: the righteous man who suffers everything.
The friends speak Proverbs' language and get it wrong. Watch how.
The whirlwind: an answer that is a presence, not an explanation.
Asaph nearly loses his faith over the same problem — and finds footing in the sanctuary.
The limits: even wisdom is vapor when death levels everything.
The landing: fear God and keep his commandments — with your one wild, fleeting life.
Moses' psalm: 'teach us to number our days, that we may get a heart of wisdom.'
Wisdom's celebration: love strong as death, in a garden that remembers Eden.
The New Testament's wisdom book: from above, peaceable, full of mercy — and lived out loud.
End where wisdom ends: everything that has breath, praising.
